commission: Afrobarometer R16 C/C author repair; one step only.
task: Return a minimal machine-readable repair patch for this exact held C-role response. The validator rejection is “role boundary: inquiries”. The accepted C role may not own I inquiries. Set only the primary response inquiries field to an empty array; preserve all claims, answer_notes, nominations, holds, grade, and packet binding unchanged. The commission’s supplementary discovery sidecar already preserves cross-stage inquiries, so do not recreate them here. Do not perform source review, regenerate content, change any other field, or claim acceptance.

evidence.quote: Were you approached by community and/or political party representatives?

claims.text: The interviewer-side item records only whether community and/or political party representatives approached the interviewer; it names no actor, timing, or content of the approach.

evidence.quote: Did you feel threatened during the interview?

claims.text: Felt threat is recorded as an interviewer report about the interview itself, so it is a fieldwork-safety trace rather than a measure of the respondent's own exposure.

evidence.quote: Were you physically threatened during the interview?

claims.text: The physical-threat item is a narrower companion to felt threat; a positive felt-threat report need not entail physical threat, and the packet gives no link to Q106C.
Honesty is an interviewer's three-point assessment of the respondent's attitude in this interview, not a verification of answer accuracy.

evidence.quote: should not be bound by laws or court decisions

claims.text: The forced-choice pits presidential exemption from laws and court decisions against presidential obedience; it is a rule-of-law position, not an observation of presidential conduct.

evidence.quote: take control of government when elected leaders abuse power

claims.text: The military item offers non-intervention against a conditional takeover justification keyed to abuse of power; agreement with takeover is a stated norm, not evidence of any intervention.

evidence.quote: once elected, [members of Parliament] do their jobs

claims.text: The paired attribution items assign responsibility for post-election accountability of legislators and of the president; the actor list is shared, so the two can be compared without assuming a single accountability model.
This item concerns anticipated community sanction of a woman candidate, distinct from Q63B's state enforcement question and from any recorded harassment event.

evidence.quote: should government and elected officials be doing more

claims.text: The item asks for an effort-level judgment (less, right amount, more) about government action on women's rights, not an assessment of whether equality currently obtains.

evidence.quote: most important for our government and society to address

claims.text: Issue priority among listed women's-rights concerns is a single nomination with an explicit none-of-these option, so it is a ranking of salience rather than a severity measure.

evidence.quote: temporarily limit democracy or democratic freedoms

claims.text: Police enforcement of health mandates is framed as a conditional, temporary limitation of freedoms during a public-health emergency; agreement is a trade-off judgment, not an endorsement of permanent policing powers.

evidence.quote: Who do you think sent us to do this interview?

claims.text: Sponsor attribution is a respondent belief over a fixed list including state, party, media, and divine senders; it records perceived provenance, not actual commissioning.

evidence.quote: Willing to participate in follow-up surveys

claims.text: Follow-up willingness is a consent-style item with a separate not-applicable state for respondents lacking a mobile number, so refusals and ineligibility are distinct.

holds.missing: No fieldwork documentation on whether sponsor attribution or approach reports were used in interviewer training, debriefs, or quality control.
holds.why: Whether these interviewer- and respondent-side reports were acted upon, rather than merely recorded, cannot be established from metadata alone.

holds.missing: No interviewer debrief or incident log linking threat reports to subsequent interview conduct or data quality.
holds.why: Any causal reading of threat reports against respondent honesty ratings remains unsupported; the packet gives only separate item stems.

holds.missing: No country-level legal or constitutional record of presidential term limits, court-obedience controversies, or military intervention history accompanies these items.
holds.why: Historical materiality of the rule-of-law and military-norm contrasts is not documented in the packet, so rival contextual readings cannot be adjudicated here.

holds.missing: No record of which public-health mandates and enforcement episodes were contemporaneous with fieldwork.
holds.why: Whether respondents were judging actual enforcement experience or a hypothetical cannot be determined from the item text.
